import pandas as pd

# File paths for source data
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_69/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_69/test_1.csv"

# Load source tables
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)  # columns: ['city', 'driver_count', 'type']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)  # columns: ['city', 'date', 'fare', 'ride_id']

# Inspect schemas:
# df0: city (str), driver_count (int), type (str)
# df1: city (str), date (str), fare (float), ride_id (int)

# Transformation plan:
# - The target schema is ['city', 'driver_count', 'type', 'date', 'fare', 'ride_id']
# - Source0 has city, driver_count, type
# - Source1 has city, date, fare, ride_id
# - We need to join these two sources on 'city' to get all columns together.
# - Since Source1 has 1187 rows and Source0 only 126 rows, and driver_count/type info is only in Source0,
#   we will do a left join of Source1 with Source0 on 'city' to bring driver_count and type into Source1 rows.
# - This assumes that each city in Source1 appears in Source0; if not, driver_count/type will be NaN.
# - The target examples show all columns filled, so we will keep only rows where driver_count and type are not null.
# - Data types will be enforced as per target schema:
#   city: string
#   driver_count: integer
#   type: string
#   date: string (keep as is)
#   fare: float
#   ride_id: integer (ride_id in source1 might be large, so use int64)

# Perform the join
df_merged = pd.merge(df1, df0, on='city', how='left')

# Drop rows where driver_count or type is missing (to match target completeness)
df_merged = df_merged.dropna(subset=['driver_count', 'type'])

# Enforce data types
df_merged['city'] = df_merged['city'].astype(str)
df_merged['driver_count'] = df_merged['driver_count'].astype(int)
df_merged['type'] = df_merged['type'].astype(str)
df_merged['date'] = df_merged['date'].astype(str)
df_merged['fare'] = df_merged['fare'].astype(float)
# ride_id might be large, convert to int64
df_merged['ride_id'] = df_merged['ride_id'].astype('int64')

# Reorder columns to match target schema
target_columns = ['city', 'driver_count', 'type', 'date', 'fare', 'ride_id']
df_target = df_merged[target_columns]

# Write to target CSV
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_69/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
